title: 2003 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: A parabola with equation \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) is reflected about the \(x\)-axis. The parabola and its reflection are translated horizontally five units in opposite directions to become the graphs of \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x),\) respectively. Which of the following describes the graph of \(y = (f + g)(x)?\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: a parabola not tangent to the \(x\)-axis

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the graph of a cubic function

solutions.text:
Write the parabola in vertex form \(y=a(x-h)^2+k.\) Its reflection about the \(x\)-axis is \(y=-a(x-h)^2-k.\)

Shifting in opposite directions gives \(f(x)=a(x-h+5)^2+k\) and \(g(x)=-a(x-h-5)^2-k.\)

Adding, the squared terms cancel and \((f+g)(x)=20a(x-h),\) which is a non-horizontal line since \(a\neq0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the parabola as \(a(x-h)^2+k;\) its reflection is \(-a(x-h)^2-k\)
After the opposite \(\pm5\) shifts, add \(f\) and \(g\) and watch the squared terms cancel
